duration_source: Complete decode of the specifically approved private Descript export

scenes.title: Keep manual progress separate from location

captions.text: This exercise follows a fictional route already started for
the assigned training unit.
In Settings, Realtime Geolocation and Background Geolocation are
off for this software exercise.
The check-ins you will see are manual status updates.
They do not demonstrate physical arrival or geofence validation.
Open Routes and find the Active Route card.
Its zero-percent progress is separate from the saved plan listed below it.

scenes.title: Open the current stop and check in

captions.text: Select Active Route.
Current Step identifies Supply point A and shows Pending.
Review the intended stop before selecting Check In.
The returned current step now says In Progress, and Check Out replaces Check In.
Progress remains zero percent because the stop is still in progress.
In operational use, follow your department’s arrival procedure
and confirm you are updating the correct assigned route.

scenes.title: Check out and verify the next pending stop

captions.text: After the first stop’s work is finished, select Check Out.
The progress display changes to fifty percent.
Current Step now identifies Community point B, with Pending
and its Check In button.
Check the name and state together.
The changed current step and percentage provide immediate feedback that the
first stop’s checkout was saved.
For Community point B, select Check In. The returned current
step now says In Progress.
Select Check Out after completing that stop’s work.
The page now shows one hundred percent and Stops Completed.
Scroll the stop list to reach End Route.
Finishing all the stop checkouts and ending the route are separate actions; the
End Route control is still available here.

scenes.title: End the execution deliberately
visual_required_labels: Are you sure you want to end this route?

captions.text: Select End Route.
Read the confirmation asking whether you want to end this route.
required_labels: Are you sure you want to end this route?

spoken_references.Are you sure you want to end this route?: confirmation asking whether you want to end this route

captions.text: Cancel leaves the execution open; confirm End Route when the assignment is finished.
After confirmation, the app returns to Routes.
The saved Community supply loop plan remains in the list, while
the Active Route card is gone.
Ending this execution has not deleted the reusable plan.

scenes.title: Verify the saved execution in Core

captions.text: An authorized supervisor can reopen the same execution in Core.
Instance Info now shows Completed, unit fifty-one thousand eight,
a Started time, an Ended time, and progress of two out of two.
Use these stored details to verify the result independently
of the Unit screen’s navigation.
The map here is not evidence of a recorded vehicle journey.
Scroll to Stop Timeline.
Each of the two recorded entries shows Completed, an In
time, an Out time, and Dwell.
These are the saved times from the manual training check-ins and checkouts.
Very short exercise dwell times are not operational travel estimates.
Review these entries when investigating an execution, while keeping your department’s
location and reporting procedures in mind.

scenes.title: Compare history and apply the workflow
visual_required_labels: Route History - TRAINING ONLY - Community supply loop

captions.text: Route History retains both completed practice executions.
required_labels: Route History - TRAINING ONLY - Community supply loop

captions.text: Compare Started and Ended to identify the intended run,
then use Detail to reopen it.
Both rows have two out of two stops completed.
This workflow can support community paramedicine visits, mental health
response logistics, search-and-rescue supply runs, security rounds, wildland
support and industrial response teams, as well as fire and E M S.
Choose meaningful stops, assign the right unit and verify saved results.
